# Policy classification

How to find a repo's AI-assisted contribution policy, classify it, cite it, and decide eligibility. Run this at gate 2. The registry may already hold a classification. Re-check the cited file anyway if it is older than a month, because policies change.

## Where to look, in order

1. **Contributor guides.** Check `CONTRIBUTING.md` at the root, in `.github/`, and in `docs/`.
2. **Org-wide files.**
   - The org's `.github` repo, which supplies a default `CONTRIBUTING.md` when the repo has none.
   - Org policy files such as an `AI_POLICY.md` that say they apply to every repo in the org.
3. **The pull request template.** Check `.github/pull_request_template.md` and `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/`.
4. **Other `.github/` files.** Issue templates, and workflows that auto-close pull requests. Search workflow files for `close` and for author-association checks.
5. **Pinned issues.** Policy announcements often live there.
6. **Agent guides.** Check `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`. These often address agents working inside the repo, not contributors, so read them as two kinds of text:
   - Lines aimed at contributors' agents, such as disclosure rules or rejection warnings, count as policy.
   - Lines aimed at the maintainers' own agents do not count as policy, but they can still constrain disclosure. One example is a ban on attribution footers.

## Classes

| Class | Test | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `allows` | An explicit line welcomes AI-assisted contributions, usually with conditions | Eligible, subject to its conditions |
| `silent` | Nothing found in any location above | Eligible; pull request descriptions carry the default prose line, comments and replies carry none |
| `bans` | An explicit line refuses AI-generated or AI-assisted contributions | Stop |

Cite the exact line with the file and line number, for example `CONTRIBUTING.md:63 "AI-assisted contributions are welcome"`. Or write `none found` and list the locations checked. A paraphrase is not a citation.

## Eligibility stops beyond `bans`

Stop even when the class is `allows` or `silent` if any of these hold. Each is an exclusion. A fuller review flow does not lift it, and the agent never fills in a human attestation on the user's behalf.

- **Attestation.** The policy requires the human owner to attest to reviewing the complete change.
- **Issues only.** The repo accepts issues but not pull requests, for example "We accept issues, not pull requests."
- **Members only.** The repo accepts pull requests only from members or staff. A workflow that auto-closes outside pull requests counts.
- **Assignment first.** Outside pull requests are reviewed only after a maintainer assigns the linked issue. This is a stop until the assignment arrives, and the intake gate handles it.

Data can also exclude a repo when no line says so. If the last 20 outside pull requests got no maintainer response and none merged, the repo is not absorbing outside work. That is the registry owner's call, recorded as status `excluded`.

## Disclosure patterns seen in practice

Record the pattern per action type in the registry, as a prose rule plus a template the poster checks: `unknown`, `none`, or one line with `{slots}`. The skill reads the template from the registry and does not guess.

- **Disclosure with extent.** "This must be disclosed in the pull request or issue, along with the extent to which AI assistance was used." Often paired with "If your PR responses or comments are being generated by an AI, disclose that as well," which covers replies too.
- **Fixed description line.** A line in which the agent names itself and links to itself, plus self-identification as automated in every comment and review. Some of these repos also require updating an existing agent comment instead of posting another. The poster only posts new comments, so such a repo stays paused.
- **Optional disclosure.** The policy welcomes AI assistance and makes disclosure optional. Record the line that says so; that is not `none found`. The registry owner picks the template, usually the same prose line as a silent repo.
- **Environment disclosure.** The model, harness, harness version, and every installed plugin, on every pull request and issue.
- **No AI attribution.** An agent guide forbids attributing commits or pull request bodies to an AI tool. Disclosure is one prose line in the body with no tool or model name, and nothing in the commits.

When a repo's lines cover pull requests but say nothing about comments, the comment format is `unknown`. An `unknown` format stops that action type until the registry owner fills it in. This applies only to repos with an explicit policy. A `silent` repo has no lines to follow, so it uses the defaults in `pr-description-template.md`: one prose line in pull request descriptions, and none on comments and replies.

## Recording the result

Give one line per repo in the Policy section of the queue item:

```
allows: CONTRIBUTING.md:63 "AI-assisted contributions are welcome" (https://...). Disclosure for issue_comment: [registry text].
```
